note: Independent re-judgment after 381e927417 against RFC 8050 Section 4.1 ("This adds a field to the RIB Entries record to store the Path Identifier when used with the RIB_IPV4_UNICAST_ADDPATH, RIB_IPV4_MULTICAST_ADDPATH, RIB_IPV6_UNICAST_ADDPATH, and RIB_IPV6_MULTICAST_ADDPATH subtypes."). The operator add-path leaf is gone: dumpRIBForMRT reads PeerRIB.IsAddPath per family, peels the 4-octet Path Identifier of every ADD-PATH key and hands the route to OnRouteAddPath, any other route to OnRoute; writeTableDumpV2 takes each record's subtype from the callback (ribSubtypeFor) and writes the Path Identifier into the RIB Entry for subtypes 8-11. Q1 (RFC, not code): TestRFC8050AddPathRIBEntryFollowsFigure1 byte-compares the literal Figure 1 octets; the writer and dump tests decode the Path Identifier at the Figure 1 position, so one written before Originated Time or after Attribute Length decodes as a wrong PathID or a wrong length. Q2 (fails on non-compliance): TestRFC8050DumpV2AddPathStoresPathID requires subtypes 8, 9, 10, 11, PathIDs 7 and 42 and a body of exactly base+4 octets on OnRouteAddPath, and base subtypes 2-5 at exactly the base length on OnRoute, on Config{} (the default). TestRFC8050MRTDumpDefaultConfigKeepsPathIDs and TestRFC8050MRTDumpMixedAddPathState drive the real RIB walk into the MRT writer on the default configuration; prefixRecord pins each body to its subtype's layout, and the mixed test's default arm fails on any record whose subtype contradicts the route's stored ADD-PATH state (peer A IPv4 ADD-PATH -> 8 with 7/42, peer A IPv6 without -> 4, peer B IPv4 without -> 2). TestRFC8050MRTSnapshotPreservesPathIDs pins the bridge for all four AFI/SAFI pairs; TestRIBRecordAddPathRoundTrip/TestRIBRecordRoundTrip pin the codec. Q3: one route per record with valid attributes, nothing else can fail first. Q4: all four subtypes are covered at writer and bridge level; the end-to-end default-configuration walk proves the ADD-PATH subtype for IPv4 unicast only (8), and the base subtype for IPv4 and IPv6 unicast (2, 4). Observation, not a finding: dumpRIBForMRT peels the Path Identifier and falls back to OnRoute when a visitor sets no OnRouteAddPath, which would lose it; the MRT writer always sets both callbacks, so no shipped path reaches it. One RIB Entry per record is permitted by RFC 8050.
